correctness.rationale: The integer-slope step follows from all iterates acting on two integer values; the ratio limit bounds index displacements and forces a unique eventual shift; a fixed positive shift makes the weighted sum of one-step drifts diverge, contradicting a constant intercept. Negative and zero slopes are fully classified. Two-term Stirling expansions apply to every positive Fuss–Catalan and fixed-slope binomial parameter, and exact recurrence/drift tests independently corroborate the algebra.

value.rationale: Complete exact affine-endomorphism classifications for the Catalan, all Fuss–Catalan and fixed-slope binomial families are natural arithmetic invariants. The ratio-plus-unbounded-drift theorem unifies these infinite families and has a sharp contrasting translated-geometric model, explaining which fine growth defect enforces rigidity; no downstream theorem is required for a nonroutine natural classification.
